Can you please provide the following by end of day tomorrow? If you already have a CSV or telemetry export, attaching that is perfect.

- Typical prompt/response token distributions (p50/p90/p99) by endpoint.

- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, on-prem requirement) that could affect placement.

If easier, drop a sample CSV and highlight the columns we should focus on. We usually produce a preliminary GPU-count estimate within 48 hours of receiving telemetry.

Alex —

Thanks for the forward and the CSV. Quick preliminary: based on their p99 token lengths (~1200) and stateful chat behavior, the KV cache pressure and memory residency push us towards an A100xTB-equivalent or H100x-heavy mix for the steady-state. High-level estimate below (very preliminary):

- Steady-state sizing (120 qps): ~6 H100-equivalent GPUs provisioned for reserved capacity to meet p99 <= 1.2s with batching and KV caching, assuming average 300-token responses for the chat mix. This includes ~25% headroom.
- Burst handling: allow burst pool of autoscaled cheaper quantized instances (e.g., 8-bit T4/GPU-equivalent nodes) with a warm buffer of 2 H100s for fast ramp. For their 12x observed peak, recommend a burst strategy that combines on-demand nodes + pre-warmed burst instances; estimate cost multiplier ~3.5x vs reserved steady-state during sustained high events (short bursts will spike less due to batching inefficiencies).
- KV cache: they should plan for ~24–32 GB/session working set for p99 long responses with multi-turn state; recommend per-GPU memory budget of 512GB effective (sharded across GPUs or using memory-optimized SKUs).

Deliverables I can produce by tomorrow EOD if we want to tighten numbers: a) preliminary GPU count/cost model (spreadsheet), b) recommended SKU mapping (H100 vs A100 vs T4 mixes), c) one-page operations note on graceful fallback and cache warm strategies.

If Alex thinks this is ready, I can attach the spreadsheet and a short note to the commercial.

—Marissa
